description:
The surah that opens with the oath of the Divine One swearing by the sky of the world and **The Nightly Visitor** so called because it comes by night and leaves by day. It takes its name from verse 1 which mentions "the night-comer" or "nightly visitor" (ṭāriq). The surah focuses on a series of examples of things coming out: the piercing night-star, spurting semen, the baby that bursts out of the womb, and plants that sprout out of the ground. All of these are used to illustrate resurrection from the grave.
The surah is also known as: The Night Star, The Night-Comer, The Night-Visitant, The Nightcomer, The Nightly Visitant, The Piercing Star.

11.1: Or 'by the sky endowed with rains.'

translations.1: By the sky, by the nightly visitor,
translations.2: (and what will show you what is the nightly visitor?
translations.4: there is a guard<{["F", 1]}> over every soul.
translations.5: So let man consider from what he was created.
translations.6: He was created from an effusing fluid
translations.7:
which issues from between the loins
  and the breast-bones.
translations.8: Indeed He is able to bring him back [after death],
translations.9: on the day when the secrets are examined,
translations.10: and he shall have neither power nor helper.
translations.13: it is indeed a decisive word,
translations.14: and it is not a jest.
translations.15: Indeed they are devising a stratagem,
translations.16: and I [too] am devising a plan.
translations.17:
So _respite_ the faithless;
  _give_ them a gentle respite.
